newsitem.title: FRANCE: French capital markets closing report.
newsitem.headline: French capital markets closing report.

text.p: Renewed confidence the Socialist victory in Sunday's French poll will not critically harm the move to a single European currency and an end to the German row about revaluing gold reserves trimmed French bond yields.

Comments from Socialist party member Elisabeth Guigou, tipped to be European Affairs minister, that the government would stick to the EMU timetable and the Communists could join the government but with no conditions helped French bonds.
Traders said more non-resident investors, positioned for a slump in the market, were forced to buy back bonds to close their positions and this boosted prices.
The June bond future opened slightly higher at 128.56 and rallied to 129.40 during the day, with the move being accelerated as stop/loss triggered and a strong rally in German bond futures.

The surge in bond futures, combined with talk of interest in long-dated cash bonds, trimmed 10-year bond yields to 5.71 percent from 5.83 percent, moving the spread below German yields to 12 basis points from nine basis points.
One trader at a French brokerage said the bond future was now at a key level and if it passed 129.40 it could head to 129.92 with another target of 130.12.
June interest rate futures also rallied on the back of short covering, a favourable backdrop from the franc and the rally at the long end of the market, traders said.

Traders said while many had positioned themselves for a slide in PIBOR contracts. The fact the franc was held relatively steady after the poll diffused the likelihood of a crisis or higher interest rates, making implied interest rates look out of line with official rates.
Implied three month interest rates fell to 3.48 percent on Tuesday from 3.82 percent the day after the first round of voting which gave the left a surprise win.

Sonja Gibbs, bond analyst at Nomura International, said the agreement between the German government and the Bundesbank to transfer profits from the revaluation of gold and currency reserves in 1998 instead of 1997 "means people are going to buy mark assets, whether sensible or not, it is almost a relief."
"This brings a narrow EMU ever so slightly back into the picture, at least from a German point of view," Gibbs said.
The head of a brokerage in Paris said domestic investor cash holdings could well support the market in the coming days even if the risks suggested the market should decline.
"Every one is short and they have to place their cash. Investors have cash, they've been patient, waited for the first round, the second. They con't wait any longer."
The Treasury announced it would sell 20-22 billion francs of OATs on Thursday, slightly less than at auctions earlier in the year, in the three lines.
